title: The lifted smaller-cover detector detects after the open unit is invertible
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with the derived localizations for module sheaves and their open restrictions [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $s$ be a finite affine open cover with $|s|\geq2$. Assume every scheme with these same hypotheses and a strictly smaller finite affine cover has a perfect quasi-coherent zero detector supported on each closed subset with quasi-compact complement [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Let $T\subseteq X$ be closed with quasi-compact complement. There exist a quasi-compact open $U$, an affine open $V$ with $X=U\cup V$, a right adjoint $R$ of derived open restriction $L$ to the localized module site on $U$, an adjunction $L\dashv R$, and a perfect quasi-coherent $Q$ supported on $T$, such that every quasi-coherent $K$ supported on $T$ with invertible adjunction unit $K\to R L K$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(Q[n],K)=0$ for all integers $n$ is zero. Support means every cohomology stalk outside $T$ is zero. No detection property is asserted without invertibility of the unit.

proof.text: Remove one affine member V from the finite cover and let U be the union of the rest. The restricted charts form a strictly smaller cover of U. Transport the given derived localizations across the canonical equivalences for U and its opens. Quasi-separatedness and compactness give the needed compact complements. Apply the induction hypothesis on U to T intersect U and obtain the supported perfect detector P.

Apply the supported perfect map-lifting theorem to the zero map P to the zero quasi-coherent object. Its source Q is perfect and supported on T, and P is a retract of its restriction to U. Local strictly perfect representatives imply that Q has quasi-coherent cohomology.

Use unbounded derived open direct image as the right adjoint R of exact restriction, transported to the localized module site. For K with invertible unit, adjunction and restriction commuting with shifts identify shifted maps from Q with maps from its restriction. The retract P gives shifted orthogonality to P. Induction makes the restriction zero; the invertible unit then makes K zero.
